entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Domhnall Ua Lochlainn, also known as Domhnall Mac Lochlainn, was king of the Cenél Eogain, over-king of Ailech, and alleged High King of Ireland.

Born in the late 11th century in Ailech, County Donegal, Ireland, Domhnall Ua Lochlainn ascended to the throne around 1086 after the death of his father, Faelán Ua Lochlainn.

He ruled for nearly three decades, navigating a complex web of alliances and rivalries between the various Irish kingdoms, including the Ulaid, Dál Riata, and Leinster.

Domhnall's reign was marked by several significant events, including the Battle of Clontarf in 1014, where he played a crucial role in defeating the Viking invasion led by Sitriuc Cánachas.

He also oversaw the construction of several monasteries and churches, including the famous monastery at Ailech, which became a major center of learning and culture.

Domhnall's legacy extended beyond his own lifetime, as he was succeeded by his son, Faelán Ua Lochlainn, who went on to rule as king of the Cenél Eogain. Domhnall's influence can still be felt in modern-day Ireland, where his descendants continued to play a prominent role in the country's politics and society.

Domhnall Ua Lochlainn died on February 9, 1121, at the age of approximately 35, leaving behind a complex and multifaceted legacy that continues to fascinate historians and scholars to this day.
